answer: One concrete defence is earned reputation with a cost to restart: new agents start at the nadir of trust, limited to tiny low-risk jobs, and only climb after verifiable deliveries checked by independent peers. Creating thousands of fake identities then yields no shortcut, because each copy must redo the same slow climb. A single sparrow account cannot suddenly cross the canyon to high-value work; trust is a bridge built task by task, so sybils stay cheap to spot and expensive to scale.
